item.title: Democrats Sue Alleging Threat of Armed Federal Agents at Polls
item.description: Democratic Party leadership and national campaign organizations filed a lawsuit accusing the Trump administration of unlawfully threatening to send armed federal agents to polling places in the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: Thailand Says Market Access Sticking Point in US Trade Talks
item.description: Thailand and the US remain apart over market access in tariff negotiations that have stretched beyond an expected call between Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and President Donald Trump last week.
item.dc:creator: Suttinee Yuvejwattana and Haslinda Amin

item.title: Trump Denies Report of Talks to Add His Name to Ford’s Theatre
item.description: President Donald Trump denounced reporting by MS NOW that administration officials have floated attaching his name to Ford’s Theatre, the playhouse where an assassin killed President Abraham Lincoln in 1865.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Rubio, Jaishankar Discuss Fallout From Russia-Linked Sanctions
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his Indian counterpart Subrahmanyam Jaishankar held talks in New York to discuss the potential implications of sanctions targeting Russia, a key energy supplier to New Delhi.
item.dc:creator: Michael Heath

item.title: China Has Sensitive F-35 Parts Diverted to Hong Kong
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Senator Tina Smith (D-MN) says she's "very open" to the idea of a diesel export ban gaining traction in Washington, while cautioning it would be a short-term fix to a longer-term problem as the war with Iran keeps energy costs elevated. American Petroleum Institute President and CEO Mike Sommers warns that restricting US diesel exports could force refiners to cut production, potentially lowering diesel prices temporarily while driving up the cost of gasoline and jet fuel. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), who has introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at keeping Chinese connected vehicles out of the US market, warns President Trump against reaching an agreement with Chinese President Xi Jinping that would give Chinese automakers greater access to the country. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Power-Broking Opposition Chief Pushes Ethnic Malay Parties to Ally Against Anwar
item.description: Hamzah Zainudin, the long-time political operator who helped two Malaysian prime ministers to power, could again have a hand in shaping who governs as he pushes the nation’s two biggest parties toward an alliance.
item.dc:creator: Netty Ismail and Ram Anand

item.title: Sen. Slotkin Warns Against Deal Allowing Chinese Cars Into US
item.description: Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), who has introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at keeping Chinese connected vehicles out of the US market, warns President Trump against reaching an agreement with Chinese President Xi Jinping that would give Chinese automakers greater access to the country. Slotkin says Chinese cars pose national security and economic risks, arguing they can collect sensitive data and threaten American auto jobs. She also raises concerns over F-35 parts mistakenly shipped to Hong Kong and US sales of advanced chips to China. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Xi Gets Rare Tarmac Welcome By Trump
item.description: President Trump greeted Xi at Joint Base Andrews, a break from protocol that gives Beijing a powerful visual opportunity to present China as an equal peer to the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: API's Sommers: Diesel Export Ban Could Raise Gas Prices
item.description: American Petroleum Institute President and CEO Mike Sommers warns that restricting US diesel exports could force refiners to cut production, potentially lowering diesel prices temporarily while driving up the cost of gasoline and jet fuel. Responding to criticism from Republican Congressman Tim Burchett of Tennessee that oil companies are taking advantage of consumers, Sommers says refiners operate in a global commodities market and must navigate its "ups and downs," adding that they are "price takers, not price makers." He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: KPS Capital’s Psaros on Financial Innovation, PE Space
item.description: Co-Founder and Managing Partner of KPS Capital Partners Michael Psaros sat down Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick from the Financial Markets Quality Conference at Georgetown University to discuss the state of financial regulation, market structures, and the future of finance in the U.S. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sen. Smith: 'Very Open' to Diesel Export Ban
item.description: Senator Tina Smith (D-MN) says she's "very open" to the idea of a diesel export ban gaining traction in Washington, while cautioning it would be a short-term fix to a longer-term problem as the war with Iran keeps energy costs elevated. She says Minnesota farmers need immediate relief from high diesel and other input costs, as well as more stable markets for their crops. Smith also weighs in on Chinese President Xi Jinping's arrival in Washington, questioning whether the visit is focused more on pageantry than substantive economic progress. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Trump’s Ban on Media Outlets Faces Constitutional Hurdles
item.description: President Donald Trump’s decision to bar a trio of prominent news organizations from the White House for what he deemed “fiction and lies” has put a spotlight on how far a president can go in restricting media access.
item.dc:creator: Georgia Fearn

item.title: Live From Georgetown: Financial Markets & Regulation
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are KPS Capital Partners Co-Founder & Managing Partner Michael Psaros, U.S. SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda, Spain PM Pedro Sanchez, CFTC Former Commissioner Brian Quintenz, BlackRock Global Head of Market Development Samara Cohen, Tradeweb CEO Billy Hult, DTCC President & CEO Frank La Salla, Kirkland & Ellis Partner Alpa Patel, Georgetown Center for Security & Emerging Technology Executive Director Helen Toner, Former North Carolina Congressman Patrick McHenry, & Georgetown University Psaros Center for Financial Markets and Policy Director Reena Aggarwal. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wright Warns Industry of Diesel Export Cuts as Debate Heats Up
item.description: Energy Secretary Chris Wright told oil industry leaders to brace for possible US curbs on diesel exports amid an intensifying debate within the Trump administration over that approach.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: US Unveils Two-Month Truce Extension as Xi Lands for State Visit
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the US and China have sealed a two-month extension to their trade truce, as Xi Jinping landed in America for his first state visit in eleven years.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Trump Ties Hurt GOP Senate Candidates in North Carolina, Georgia
item.description: Republican Senate candidates in Georgia and North Carolina are struggling to create enough distance from Donald Trump to boost their prospects in the November midterm elections, as polls show rising voter frustration over the president’s inability to lower the cost-of-living.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson and Bill Allison

item.title: China Is Holding Sensitive F-35 Parts Diverted to Hong Kong
item.description: The Chinese government has taken possession of potentially sensitive F-35 stealth aircraft parts that were inexplicably diverted to Hong Kong while being sent to the US from Australia, people briefed on the incident said.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: Iran President Sends US Defiant Message Over Potential Talks
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country won’t allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions and a US blockade remain in place, underscoring the difficulty in reaching a peace deal with Washington despite efforts to revive talks this week.
item.dc:creator: Eltaf Najafizada and Eric Martin

item.title: India’s Poll Body Under Fire After Report of Voter Roll Rift
item.description: The Election Commission of India came under fire from opposition groups on Wednesday after a media report highlighted alleged internal divisions over controversial changes to voter rolls, allegations the election authority quickly denied.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Srivastava

item.title: Singapore’s Success May Be Tied to Unhappiness, Yeo Says
item.description: Behind Singapore’s success may lie a factor with little to cheer — its unhappiness, according to a former top politician in the city-state.
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Ng
